name: FormLayout
description: Groups form fields with even, tokenized spacing: vertical stack, horizontal row, or 1-4 column grid, optionally as a semantic fieldset.
designIntent: Field rhythm is the difference between a form that scans and one that doesn't. FormLayout owns the ARRANGEMENT (stack/row/grid + exact gap) while Fieldset owns the group semantics (legend) and FormField owns per-control wiring — three small pieces instead of one magic wrapper.

props.name: layout
props.description: Grouping layout: even vertical stack, horizontal row, or column grid.

props.name: columns
props.description: Grid column count (literal classes survive CSS purging).

props.name: gap
props.description: Even spacing between children — token or exact pixels (16).

props.name: legend
props.description: Group label rendered as a semantic <legend> (fieldset mode).

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting line under the legend (fieldset mode).

props.name: as
props.description: Render as a semantic fieldset when the layout names a group of controls.

examples.title: Two-column settings grid
examples.code:
<FormLayout layout="grid" columns={2} gap={16} as="fieldset" legend="Profile">
  <FormField id="first" label="First name"><Input /></FormField>
  <FormField id="last" label="Last name"><Input /></FormField>
  <FormField id="email" label="Email"><Input type="email" /></FormField>
</FormLayout>
examples.description: Exact 16px gaps; fields wrap into rows of two.

examples.title: Inline action row
examples.code:
<FormLayout layout="row" gap="sm">
  <FormField id="q" label="Search"><Input type="search" /></FormField>
  <Button type="submit">Go</Button>
</FormLayout>

antiPatterns.title: Don't hand-roll spacer divs
antiPatterns.explanation: Empty divs with heights drift from the token scale and break under different densities — gap exists for spacing.

antiPatterns.title: Don't use fieldset mode without a legend
antiPatterns.explanation: as="fieldset" without legend renders an unnamed group — assistive tech announces nothing useful. Prefer div, or provide the legend.

accessibility.feature: Fieldset mode gives the group a name
accessibility.implementation: legend renders as a real <legend>; use it whenever the layout wraps related controls
accessibility.userRequirements: Legend text must name the choice, not the layout

accessibility.implementation: Row/grid layouts reflow visually; source order never changes
accessibility.userRequirements: Order fields by task flow, not visual position

compositionRules.relationship: FormLayout arranges the fields; each field keeps its own FormField wiring
Layouts live inside a Form (or standalone for filter bars)
Fieldset when the legend/grouping IS the point; FormLayout when spacing/arrangement is
